content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, tracing each element back to the disclosure.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 17 claims (independents 1, 11, 14 and dependents 2-10, 12-13, 15-17) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (semicircular halves, hinge/latch ends, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads with no tool-specific diameter, segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per half, complementary drive faces at hinge and latch ends coupling on closure, follower in oblique slot, wedge on latch against a ring drive face, limited stroke, synchronized inward travel, carriage springs, first/over-center latch positions, force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing in a predetermined compression range, mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization, and the install/remove sequence). All 28 numerals (10-26, 30-66) were checked: each designates exactly one part, each appears in at least one figure brief and in the description, and every figure cross-reference in draft/08 (FIGS. 2 and 5 for carriages, FIG. 2 for the annular guide, FIG. 3 for the segments, FIGS. 3 and 4 for the ring drive face, FIG. 5 for follower and slot, FIG. 6 for the four segment end faces, FIG. 4 for the latch parts) matches the brief that carries that numeral. Segment/half/junction orientation is internally consistent across FIGS. 1, 3 and 6 (12 upper with 32, 14 lower with 34, hinge and 44/46 at the left junction, latch and 48/50 and the ring drive face 54 at the right junction), and FIG. 5's inner-is-lower convention matches the uppermost carriage of FIG. 2. No section lines are designated in any view, so no section-designation mismatch exists. The application text contains no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative, "by way of example" shape hedge, "any closed outline" language, or means-plus-function limitation; the title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support statements match input/brief.md; the abstract is a single paragraph under 150 words; and the Background contains only prior-art characterizations with no reference citations, so no citation issues arise. Four defects are reported, all in the figure briefs. One is a critical source-fidelity defect: FIG. 4 verbalizes an undisclosed port and projection for the indicator pin ("passes through the top wall of the housing, with its upper end projecting above the housing") and re-labels numeral 60, which the ledger and description call the "fixed edge", as "the top wall of the housing"; the source says only that a visible pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing, so the wall chosen, the through-passage and the external projection are untraced statements about a functional read-out interface. The remaining three are internal-consistency defects: numerals 18 (releasable latch) and 58 (latch housing) in FIG. 4 both target the latch-housing wall with no separation instruction, so 18 does not resolve to one thing; numeral 30 in FIG. 3 may terminate on the same band region as 32 or 34 with no separation instruction (FIG. 1 handles the analogous 10 vs. 12/14 case correctly by requiring separation); and FIG. 5 draws the carriage "narrower than the slideway", asserting clearance at the sliding joint that the source describes as a carriage that slides in a radial guide. Note for the record: the drafting agent's own passage in input/conversation.md claims the invention turns on a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" - that passage is agent prose, not inventor support, and nothing of the kind appears anywhere in the draft, which is correct. No prior-art files were supplied with this material, so the art considered may be incomplete; that does not affect this preflight, which assesses only source fidelity and internal consistency.

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief adds an undisclosed top-wall passage and external projection for the indicator pin
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md - View paragraph, Geometry to draw (fifth bullet), and numeral placement targets for 60 and 64
findings.detail: The brief specifies that the indicator pin "passes through the top wall of the housing, with its upper end projecting above the housing", that the view must accommodate "the projecting upper end of the indicator pin", that numeral 64 marks "the part of the indicator pin that projects above the housing", and that numeral 60 - which the numeral ledger and draft/08 call the "fixed edge" - marks "the top wall of the housing beside the indicator pin". No affirmative inventor passage discloses a top wall, a passage through a wall, a pin end projecting above the housing, or an identification of the fixed edge with a top wall. The indicator pin and the fixed edge form a functional read-out interface, so which wall carries the pin, whether the pin penetrates that wall, and how far it stands proud of the housing are substantive statements about a port and its end position, not neutral outline choices, even though the brief says the components are "shown schematically". The brief also renames numeral 60 away from the designation used everywhere else in the application.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "A slender indicator pin passes through the top wall of the housing, with its upper end projecting above the housing."; "60: the top wall of the housing beside the indicator pin."; "64: the part of the indicator pin that projects above the housing." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md), which shows the gap: "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range." The disclosure never mentions a top wall, a through-passage, or a projecting pin end; draft/08 states only "An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, replace the fifth geometry bullet with: "A slender indicator pin is carried at the latch housing so that a portion of the pin is visible outside the housing next to an edge of the housing; the pin and that edge are shown schematically." In the View paragraph, replace "including the projecting upper end of the indicator pin and the free end of the handle" with "including the visible portion of the indicator pin and the free end of the handle". Replace the numeral targets with: "60: the edge of the latch housing next to the visible portion of the indicator pin." and "64: the visible portion of the indicator pin outside the housing." No change is needed to draft/08, draft/07 or the claims, which already recite only a fixed edge of the latch housing.

findings.title: FIG. 4 gives numerals 18 and 58 the same target, so the latch numeral does not resolve to one part
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md - numeral placement targets for 18 and 58
findings.detail: Numeral 18 is the releasable latch and numeral 58 is the latch housing, but both placement targets point at the same line work - the outer boundary/wall of the latch housing - and both are qualified only by being clear of the indicator pin (and, for 18, the handle and wedge). Nothing in the brief separates the two leader terminations, so the two leaders can land on the same housing line and a reader cannot tell which numeral designates the assembly and which the housing. FIG. 1 handles the analogous whole-versus-part case correctly by requiring numeral 10 on the outer boundary and 12 and 14 "well inside" the halves, "away from the outer boundary"; FIG. 4 omits any such separation.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "18: the outer boundary of the latch housing, at a place clear of the handle, of the wedge and of the indicator pin." and "58: the wall of the latch housing, clear of the indicator pin." Ledger (draft/numerals.md): "| 18 | releasable latch |" and "| 58 | latch housing |" - two distinct parts. Compare figures/FIG-1.md, which separates the whole from its parts: "10: the outer boundary of the annular frame body..."; "12: well inside the upper frame half, away from the outer boundary."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, replace the 18 target with: "18: the latch as a whole, its leader terminating on the outline of the latch at a point clearly spaced from the termination of the 58 leader and clear of the handle, the wedge, the spring stack and the indicator pin." and replace the 58 target with: "58: the wall of the latch housing, clear of the indicator pin and clearly spaced from the termination of the 18 leader."

findings.title: FIG. 3 allows numeral 30 to terminate on the same band region as numeral 32 or 34
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md - numeral placement targets for 30, 32 and 34
findings.detail: Numeral 30 is the cam ring and numerals 32 and 34 are the two segments that wholly constitute it. The brief directs 30 to "the ring band" and 32 and 34 to "the band of the upper arcuate segment" and "the band of the lower arcuate segment", with the only qualifiers being clearance from the slots, junctions and drive face. Because every point of the band belongs to one segment or the other, the 30 leader can terminate immediately beside the 32 or 34 leader on the same band, leaving it ambiguous whether that band is being called the ring or the segment. FIG. 1 avoids the same problem for 10 versus 12 and 14 by specifying spatial separation.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "30: the ring band, at a place clear of the slots, the junctions and the drive face."; "32: the band of the upper arcuate segment, clear of the slots and of both junctions."; "34: the band of the lower arcuate segment, clear of the slots and of both junctions." Draft/08: "the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34" - 30 has no territory of its own on the band.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, replace the 30 target with: "30: the ring band, its leader terminating at a point clearly spaced from the terminations of the 32 and 34 leaders and clear of the slots, the junctions and the drive face."

findings.title: FIG. 5 draws the carriage narrower than its slideway, asserting undisclosed clearance at the sliding joint
findings.where: figures/FIG-5.md - Geometry to draw, second bullet
findings.detail: The brief instructs that the carriage be drawn "narrower than the slideway, centered in the slideway", which depicts a gap on both sides between the carriage and the guide walls. The carriage-in-guide interface is a sliding joint, and whether the carriage bears on the guide walls is contact topology, which remains substantive notwithstanding the brief's "shown schematically" note. The only source statement is that each carriage slides in a radial guide, i.e. that the guide constrains the carriage; no inventor passage discloses a loose or clearance fit.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-5.md): "A carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway, centered in the slideway." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md): "Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad..." Draft/08 likewise states only: "The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame." Neither discloses clearance between the carriage and the guide walls.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-5.md, replace the second geometry bullet with: "A carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle whose two sides run along the two parallel lines of the slideway, so that the carriage is guided by the slideway, shown schematically."
